children.title: Why one, none or infinitely many?
children.summary: Moves two lines: crossing, parallel or identical (spec below)
children.spec: Two lines: drag the slopes and intercepts; the solution counter shows 1, 0 or ∞. Algebra mirror: elimination run live; parallel lines produce 0 = 5, identical lines produce 0 = 0. Three planes: a 3D view of the same three cases plus 'pairwise crossings with no common point'. Determinant hint: det = 0 exactly when the lines are parallel or identical (see the determinants box).

children.title: Why does elimination work?
children.summary: Adds equations; the new line still passes through the same intersection

children.title: Three equations = three planes
children.summary: Rotates three planes in 3D: a point, a line, or no common point

children.title: Substitution versus elimination
children.summary: Solves one system both ways

children.title: Ticket and mixture problems
children.summary: Turns the story into two equations

children.title: Why is a matrix just the equations?
children.summary: Strips out the letters and keeps the numbers in place

children.title: Why don't row operations change the answer?
children.summary: Sees each operation as a legal move on the equations, with the solution point fixed

children.title: Row-reduction stepper
children.summary: Reaches echelon form one operation at a time

children.title: Spot inconsistent and dependent systems
children.summary: Reads a 0 = 1 row or a free variable

children.title: Why 'row times column'?
children.summary: Substitutes one linear system into another; the product appears (Cayley's original reason)

children.title: Why is AB not BA?
children.summary: Applies 'rotate then shear' versus 'shear then rotate' to a square

children.title: Why do some matrices have no inverse?
children.summary: Watches a matrix squash the plane onto a line, which can't be undone

children.title: Why does (AB)′ = B′A′ reverse the order?
children.summary: Transposes a product entry by entry and sees row i of A meet column j of B swap roles

children.title: Why does every square matrix split into symmetric + skew-symmetric parts?
children.summary: Averages A with its mirror A′ to get the symmetric part ½(A + A′); the leftover ½(A − A′) flips sign when mirrored, so its diagonal is 0

children.title: Multiply matrices step by step
children.summary: Highlights each row–column pair

children.title: Inverse by [A | I]
children.summary: Row-reduces to get A⁻¹, then solves AX = B

children.title: Matrix types spotter
children.summary: Sorts matrices into row, column, square, diagonal, scalar, identity and zero

children.title: Matrix secret codes
children.summary: Encodes a message with a matrix and decodes it with the inverse

children.title: A shop's bill as a matrix product
children.summary: Multiplies a quantities matrix by a price matrix to total several customers' bills at once

children.title: Why is the determinant an area?
children.summary: Sees the columns span a parallelogram whose area is |det|

children.title: Why does det = 0 mean trouble?
children.summary: Sees zero area means flattened, so no unique solution

children.title: Why does Cramer's rule work?
children.summary: Swaps a column and compares areas

children.title: Why is A (adj A) = |A| I?
children.summary: Multiplies a row by its own cofactors (gives |A|) and by another row's cofactors (gives 0: the determinant of a matrix with two equal rows)

children.title: Why is |AB| = |A| |B|?
children.summary: Applies two area-scalings one after another: the factors multiply

children.title: 2 × 2 and 3 × 3 determinants
children.summary: Expands by minors with the signs shown

children.title: Cramer's rule solver
children.summary: Solves 2- and 3-variable systems

children.title: Minors, cofactors and the adjoint
children.summary: Builds adj A and then A⁻¹ = adj A / |A| for a 3 × 3 matrix

children.title: Solve AX = B by X = A⁻¹B
children.summary: Decides consistent or inconsistent from |A| and (adj A)B, then solves

children.title: Collinear points: zero area
children.summary: Shows three points are collinear when the area determinant is 0

children.title: Triangle area from coordinates
children.summary: Uses ½|det| with three dragged vertices

children.title: How many times can two curves meet?
children.summary: Moves a line across a circle (0, 1, 2 meetings) and two conics (up to 4, as Bézout predicted)

children.summary: Tries without them and fails to match

children.summary: Covers the four cases: linear, repeated, quadratic and repeated quadratic factors

children.title: Why does a linear inequality shade a half-plane?
children.summary: Tests a point; one side of the line is all-true

children.summary: Slides the profit line across the feasible region; it leaves at a vertex

children.summary: Slides the objective line Z = k outward and checks whether the half-plane Z < k meets the region

children.title: Graph a system of inequalities
children.summary: Overlaps shaded regions to get the feasible region

children.title: Corner-point method stepper
children.summary: Finds the vertices, evaluates Z at each and checks the unbounded case
